skill.name: database-optimizer
skill.description: Expert database optimizer specializing in modern performance tuning, query optimization, and scalable architectures.
skill.summary: Improve database speed, scalability, reliability, and cost through measured query, index, caching, schema, and architecture guidance.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Slow queries and weak database designs can raise latency, cost, and operational risk. This skill provides evidence-based guidance for queries, indexes, caching, scaling, migrations, and monitoring.
actual_capabilities: Analyzes execution plans and recommends query rewrites for relational, NoSQL, cloud, and specialized databases.
Designs composite, covering, partial, full-text, spatial, and platform-specific indexing strategies.
Diagnoses N+1 queries and recommends batching, eager loading, DataLoader, or ORM changes.
Proposes caching, partitioning, sharding, replication, connection pooling, and transaction improvements.
Defines performance baselines, benchmarks, monitoring metrics, migration validation, and rollback criteria.
limitations: Provides guidance only and does not connect to databases or apply changes.
Recommendations depend on accurate schemas, query plans, workload metrics, and operational constraints.
Platform-specific syntax and behavior require validation in a representative environment.
The referenced detailed implementation playbook is not included in this package.

use_cases.title: Resolve Production Query Latency
use_cases.description: Review slow queries, execution plans, locks, and metrics to identify prioritized improvements with validation steps.

use_cases.title: Remove Application N+1 Queries
use_cases.description: Analyze ORM or GraphQL query patterns and design batching, eager-loading, or caching changes.

use_cases.title: Plan Database Growth
use_cases.description: Compare partitioning, replicas, sharding, caching, and cloud scaling options against workload and cost requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Slow Query
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this slow query for [database]. Explain likely bottlenecks and suggest safe improvements using [query, schema, and execution plan].
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one slow query

prompt_templates.title: Design an Index Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Design indexes for [table schema] and [frequent queries]. Explain column order, expected benefits, write costs, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose N+1 Behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose N+1 behavior in [framework] using [query log]. Recommend batching or eager-loading changes and a regression test.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Scaling Roadmap
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a phased scaling plan for [workload metrics], covering partitioning, replicas, caching, migration safety, observability, cost, and rollback criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced architecture planning for sustained growth

output_examples.input: A PostgreSQL order lookup is slow despite an index on customer_id.
output: Finding: filters on status and created_at may force the single-column index to scan many rows.
Recommendation: test a composite index ordered by equality and range predicates with EXPLAIN ANALYZE.
Validation: compare latency, rows scanned, index size, and write overhead before deployment.

output_examples.input: A GraphQL products page issues one inventory query per product.
output: Finding: field-level inventory loading creates an N+1 query pattern.
Recommendation: batch inventory requests by product identifier and cache results within each request.
Validation: assert a bounded query count and compare response latency under representative load.

output_examples.input: A write-heavy events table is growing beyond current maintenance windows.
output: Plan: baseline ingestion, retention, query patterns, storage growth, and maintenance duration.
Options: compare time partitioning, archival, compression, and read replicas against operational requirements.
Rollout: test one partition interval, monitor write amplification, and retain a documented rollback path.

best_practices: Capture latency, throughput, resource use, and execution plans before recommending changes.
Test optimizations with representative data and load before production deployment.
Document expected benefits, operational costs, monitoring signals, and rollback criteria.
anti_patterns: Do not add indexes without checking workload frequency, selectivity, storage, and write overhead.
Do not rewrite queries without comparing execution plans and measured results.
Do not introduce caching, sharding, or denormalization before defining consistency and invalidation requirements.

faq.question: Which databases does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers major relational, NoSQL, cloud, time-series, graph, search, and columnar database platforms described in the skill.

faq.question: Can it connect to my database?
faq.answer: No. It analyzes the schemas, plans, logs, metrics, and constraints that you provide.

faq.question: What inputs produce useful recommendations?
faq.answer: Provide the database version, schema, query, execution plan, data volume, workload pattern, current metrics, and operational constraints.

faq.question: Does it replace performance testing?
faq.answer: No. Every recommendation requires testing with representative data, concurrency, and production-like resource limits.

faq.question: Can it help plan safe migrations?
faq.answer: Yes. It can propose phased migration, monitoring, validation, rollback, and zero-downtime strategies.

faq.question: How are recommendations prioritized?
faq.answer: Recommendations prioritize measured bottlenecks, expected impact, implementation risk, maintainability, scalability, and cost.
